full_judgment:
A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J: This Rule was issued under section 115(1) C.P.C. at the instance of the petitioner calling in question an order passed by the learned District Judge admitting Election Tribunal Appeal No. 5 of 1989 preferred by the opposite party from an order rejecting an application filed under Order 47, rule 1 C.P.C. by the Election Tribunal in Misc. Case No. 1 of 1989. 

 2. The facts are: The petitioner on various allegations including the allegation of casting of false votes in the Election of Chairman of Rangamati Union Parishad filed Election Tribunal Case No. 4 of 1988 before the Election Tribunal, Fatikchari Upazila, Chittagong. The opposite party herein contested the said Election Case by filing written objection refuting the allegations made by the petitioner. The opposite party also made certain allegations of corruption, etc. practised during the poll in respect of Ward Nos. 2 and 3 of the said Union Parishad. The petitioner filed an application for striking out the allegations in respect of Ward Nos. 2 and 3 and the Tribunal by its order dated 15.12.1988 struck off allegations from the written objection. This order was challenged in Writ Petition No.1 of 1989 by the opposite party before a Division Bench of this Division. However, the same was dismissed for non- prosecution. Thereafter, the opposite party made an unsuccessful attempt before the Chief Election Commissioner to get the Election Tribunal Case transferred from the Election Tribunal, Fatikchari to some other Election Tribunal. Being unsuccessful before the Election Commission he filed an application under Order 47, rule 1 C.P.C. before the Election Tribunal, Fatikchari for reviewing the order dated 15.12.1988 striking out the allegation and Election Misc. Case No.1 of 1989 was started. The Tribunal, however holding that there was no ground for review as prescribed under Order 47, rule 1, rejected the application by its order dated 19.2.1989. That order was appealed in Election Tribunal Appeal No. 5 of 1989 before the District Judge and the District Judge by his order dated 28.2.1989 registered the appeal and called for the records fixing 1.4.1989 for hearing. This order has given rise to the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Salimul Hoque Khan Milky appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned District Judge had no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal from an order passed by the Tribunal upon an application filed under Order 47, rule 1 C.P.C. The learned Counsel placing reliance upon section 29 (4) of the Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 submits that sub-section (4) provides for an appeal from the decision of the Election Tribunal in the Election case itself and no appeal lies to the District Judge from an order which does not decide the election dispute itself. He further submits that the order appealed before the learned District Judge is not an appealable order within the meaning of Order 43, rule l(w) C.P.C. inasmuch as the order appealed before the learned District Judge is not an order granting review. 

 4. Mr. Muhammad Faiz, the learned Advocate opposes this Rule seriously on several counts. He firstly, submits that in view of the averments made in the main election petition by amendment it was necessary for the opposite party to make allegation of corruption and other allegations with regard to Ward Nos. 2 and 3 and in that view of the matter the Election Tribunal was wrong in striking out the allegations made in respect of these Wards as consideration of those allegations by the Tribunal was necessary for deciding the result of the election. Secondly, the order impugned before the District Judge being final in that by the same order the application for review was rejected and from such order appeal lies before him and the provisions of Order 43, rule 1 has no role to play in this case. Thirdly, by impugned order the learned District Judge neither had decided the appeal on merit nor has stayed the proceeding of the election case pending before the Election Tribunal and as such no injustice has been caused to either of the parties to the proceeding and in that view of the matter the application under section 115(1) C.P.C. being premature the Rule is liable to be set aside. 

 From a careful reading of the provision of section 29 it seems to me that the expressions "decision" and "on a petition" occurring in sub-section (3) of section 29 seems to me that expression "decision" means decision of the Election dispute on merit because the decision refers to "on a petition". The word "petition" used in Sub-section (3) is very significant. It seems to me that it does not admit of any other petition other than the election petition itself. This view also gets support from Sub-section (4) which refers to "announcement of the decision". "Announcement of the decision" means announcement of decision on the election dispute after hearing the parties finally. I can not read into the provision of section 29(4) any appeal other than an appeal from the final decision of the Election Tribunal on the election petition itself. Therefore my considered opinion is that an order upon an application under Order 47, rule 1 C.P.C. is not a decision within the meaning of sub-section (4) of section 29 and does not relate to certain dispute on merits more so in view of the expression 'final' used in sub-sections (3) and sub-section (4) of section 29. The decision cited by Mr. Milky in the case of Amelendu Majumder Vs. Selimuzzaman, 7 B.L.D. 114 also supports the view. I have been taken through the decision which was given on an interlocutory order passed by the Election Tribunal regarding recounting of ballot papers by the Tribunal. In the instant case before me the learned District Judge also committed an error in entertaining the present appeal from an order rejecting the review contrary to the provision of Order 43, rule 1 clause (w) inasmuch as no appeal lies under Order 43, rule 1(w) C.P.C. from an order of rejection of an application for review. 

 6. As I have held that an appeal lies to the District Judge from an order of rejection of a review petition under section 29(4) of the Ordinance, the learned District Judge acted without jurisdiction in entertaining the appeal and in making the impugned order. In view of my aforesaid discussions none of the contentions raised by the opposite party has any substance for the reasons that the first contention relates to the merit of the election case itself and thus is beyond the scope of this Rule, the second and third contentions relating to the question of jurisdiction of the learned District Judge to entertain the appeal find answer in the foregoing discussion.
